scope: Proposition 21.2 (Existence and exhaustion) of the manuscript “Boundary graph deformations for the spacetime Penrose inequality” (preprints/Boundary-graph-deformations-for-the-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4205f51d8f1b130b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 147. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the fixed strict data and every 0 < ϵ < 1 there are N0 and Rmin(N), with Rmin(N) → ∞, such that for every integer N ≥ N0 and every R ≥ Rmin(N) the desired coupled system has a smooth solution on ΩR with t > −ϵ. At each such fixed N, a subsequence as R → ∞ converges smoothly on compact subsets of Ω to a solution of the equations and inner boundary conditions with t ≥ −ϵ. The previously proved height, range and collar estimates hold for this limit.
